<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
Let $P$ and $Q$ be finite ordered sets where $\operatorname{h}(P)\le1$.  If $P^P\cong Q^Q$, then $P\cong Q$.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
Let $A$ and $B$ be finite ordered sets such that $A$ is connected.  Then $\mathcal C(A^B)$ is connected.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
Let $P$ and $Q$ be finite, disconnected ordered sets.  Assume that $\phi:P^P\to Q^Q$ is an order-isomorphism. If $Q$ has a connected component of height $\operatorname{h}(Q)$ that is directly irreducible, then $\operatorname{h}(Q)\le\operatorname{h}(P)$ and $|P|\le|Q|$.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
Let $P$ and $Q$ be finite ordered sets.  Assume $P^P\cong Q^Q$.   If $P$ has a connected component of maximum height that is directly irreducible and so does $Q$, then $\operatorname{h}(Q)=\operatorname{h}(P)$ and $|P|=|Q|$. \qed
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- observation-1: body_md -->
Let $P$ be a finite ordered set.  Let $a$ be the number of elements of height $\operatorname{h}(P)$ in $P$ and let $c$ be the number of connected components of $P$.
Then the number of elements of $P^P$ of maximum height is $a^c$.
<!-- end observation-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
Let $A$ and $B$ be finite connected ordered sets.  Then $\operatorname{h}\big(\mathcal C(B^A)\big)=\operatorname{h}(B^A)$.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
Let $P$ and $Q$ be finite ordered sets and let 
$$
\varphi:P^P\cong Q^Q.
$$
\noindent Let $k,\ell,m,n$ be such that $1\le k\le m$ and $1\le\ell\le n$; let $P_1,\dots,P_m$ be the $m$ connected components of $P$ such that $P_1,\dots,P_k$ are the components of height $\operatorname{h}(P)$; let $Q_1,\dots,Q_n$ be the $n$ connected components of $Q$ such that $Q_1,\dots,Q_\ell$ are the components of height $\operatorname{h}(Q)$.

For $f\in P^P$ and $i\in\{1,\dots,m\}$, let $\kappa(f,i)\in\{1,\dots,m\}$ be such that $f[P_i]\subseteq P_{\kappa(f,i)}$; similarly, define $\lambda(g,j)$ for $g\in Q^Q$ and $j\in\{1,\dots,n\}$.

Then $\varphi$ restricts to an order-isomorphism from
$$
\mathcal A:=\{f\in(P_1\cup\cdots\cup P_k)^P\mid\text{ for }i=1,\dots,m\text{, }f\restriction_{P_i}\in\mathcal C(P_{\kappa(f,i)}^{P_i})\}
$$ 
\noindent onto
$$
\mathcal B:=\{g\in(Q_1\cup\cdots\cup Q_\ell)^Q\mid\text{ for }j=1,\dots,n\text{, }g\restriction_{Q_j}\in\mathcal C(Q_{\lambda(g,j)}^{Q_j})\}.
$$
The ordered set $\mathcal A$ is canonically order-isomorphic to
$$
\sum_{\psi:\{1,\dots,m\}\to\{1,\dots,k\}}\prod_{i=1}^m\mathcal C(P_{\psi(i)}^{P_i}).
$$

Also, $k^m=\ell^n$.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
Let all be as in Proposition 2.7.  Assume $P_1$ and $Q_1$ are directly irreducible.  Then $m=n$ and the summand corresponding to the function $\psi:\{1,\dots,m\}\to\{1,\dots,k\}$ such that $\psi(r)=1$ for all $r\in\{1,\dots,m\}$ is such that, via Hashimoto's Strong Refinement Theorem, $\mathcal C(P_1^{P_1})\cong\mathcal C(Q_t^{Q_j})$ for some $j,t\in\mathbb N$ where $1\le t\le\ell$ and $1\le j\le n$ and $P_1\cong Q_j\cong Q_t$.
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
Let $P$ and $Q$ be finite ordered sets such that $P^P\cong Q^Q$.  Assume that $P$ has a connected component of height $\operatorname{h}(P)$ that is directly irreducible and $Q$ has a connected component of height $\operatorname{h}(Q)$ that is directly irreducible.

Then $P$ and $Q$ have the same height and the same number of connected components of maximum height, the same number of connected components, the same number of elements, and the same number of elements of height $\operatorname{h}(P)$.

There is a bijection between the set of directly-irreducible connected components of $P$ of height $\operatorname{h}(P)$ and the set of those of $Q$ that pairs order-isomorphic components.

Further, every component of $P$ of maximum height that is a product of exactly two directly-irreducible ordered sets is order-isomorphic to a connected component of $Q$, and vice versa.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
A finite, connected ordered set $P$ of height at most $1$ is either $\bf1$ or directly irreducible.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
Let $P$ and $Q$ be finite ordered sets and let $\phi:P^P\to Q^Q$ be an order-isomorphism.  Then $\operatorname{h}(P)=\operatorname{h}(Q)$ if $\operatorname{h}(P)\in\{0,1\}$.  If $\operatorname{h}(P)=2$, then either $\operatorname{h}(Q)=2$, or else $\operatorname{h}(Q)=3$ and every component $S$ of $Q$ of height $\operatorname{h}(Q)$ has the form ${\bf2}\times R_S$ where $R_S$ is a component of $P$ of height $2$.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
A finite, connected, height $1$ ordered set is absolutely $\mathcal C$-indecomposable.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
Let $P$ and $Q$ be finite ordered sets such that 
$$
P^P\cong Q^Q.
$$
\noindent  Assume that $P$ has a connected component of height $\operatorname{h}(P)$ that is absolutely $\mathcal C$-indecomposable and $Q$ has a connected component of height $\operatorname{h}(Q)$ that is directly irreducible.  Then $P\cong Q$.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
Let $A$ be an ordered set.  Then any connected component of $\widetilde A$ is either a singleton or of the form $\widetilde B$ for some ordered set $B$.
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- observation-2: body_md -->
Let $A$ be an ordered set such that $\widetilde A$ is connected and $A$ has a minimal element (equivalently, $\widetilde A$ has a minimal element).  Then $\widetilde A$ is directly irreducible.
<!-- end observation-2 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
If $P$ and $Q$ are finite ordered sets and ${\widetilde P}^{\widetilde P}\cong{\widetilde Q}^{\widetilde Q}$, then $P\cong Q$.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- notation-1: body_md -->
\rm For the rest of this section, let $P$ and $\overline P$ be finite ordered sets.  (Notions that we define for $P$, when applied to $\overline P$, will have an overbar.) Let $n:=|P|$ and $h:=\operatorname{h}(P)$.  Let $D=\{d_0,d_1,\dots,d_{nh}\}$ be a maximum-sized chain in $P^P$ where $d_0>d_1>\dots>d_{nh}$.  For 
$$
i\in\{0,1,\dots,nh-1\}\text{,}
$$
\noindent let $p_i\in P$ be such that $d_i(p_i)\gtrdot d_{i+1}(p_i)$.  For $p\in P$, let
$$
C_p:=\{d_i(p)\mid 0\le i\le nh\}\text{,}
$$
\noindent a chain of height $h$ in $P$ (from the way one proves \cite[Lemma 15(4)]{FarBC}) with top element $1_{C_p}$ and bottom element $0_{C_p}$.  For $i\in\{0,1,\dots,nh\}$, let
$$
D_i:=\{f\in P^P\mid f\ge d_i\text{ and } f(p)\in C_p\text{ for all }p\in P\}\text{;}
$$
\noindent for $i\in\{0,1,\dots,nh-1\}$, define $a_i:P\to P$ inductively for all $p\in P$ (we show it is well-defined later) by
$$
a_i(p)=\begin{cases}
d_i(p_i)\ \text{if}\ p=p_i\text{;}\\
\max\{x\in C_p\mid x\le d_{i+1}(p_i)\text{ and }x\le a_i(q)\\
\qquad\qquad\text{ for all }q\in\downarrow p_i\text{ such that }p\lessdot q\}\ \text{if}\  p<p_i\text{;}\\
1_{C_p}\ \text{if}\ p\nleq p_i\text{;}
\end{cases}
$$
\noindent and define $b_i:=(a_i)_{p_i\mapsto d_{i+1}(p_i)}$.
<!-- end notation-1 -->
<!-- observation-3: body_md -->
For $p,q\in P$ such that $p<q$, we have $0_{C_p}=0_{C_q}$ and $1_{C_p}=1_{C_q}$.
<!-- end observation-3 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
Let $i\in\{0,1,\dots,nh\}$.  Then the join and meet of every pair of elements in $D_i$ exist in $P^P$.  Indeed, $D_i$ is a bounded distributive lattice with least element $d_i$.  For $e,f\in D_i$, $p\in P$, $(e\vee f)(p)=\max\{e(p),f(p)\}$ and $(e\wedge f)(p)=\min\{e(p),f(p)\}$.
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
There is an order-embedding from $D_{nh}$ into ${\bf (h+1)}^P$.  It is an order-isomorphism if $|\{C_p\mid p\in P\}|=1$.
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
Let $i\in\{0,1,\dots,nh-1\}$.  The function $a_i$ is well-defined and $a_i\in D_i$.  It has a unique lower cover $b$ in $P^P$ such that $b\ngeq d_i$ but $b\ge d_{i+1}$, namely $b_i$.

Moreover, $b_i\wedge e$ exists in $P^P$ for all $e\in D_i$ and
$$
D_{i+1}=D_i\cup\{b_i\wedge e\mid e\in D_i\}.
$$

If $|\{C_p\mid p\in P\}|=1$, then $a_i(p)=d_{i+1}(p_i)$ for all $p\in\overset{\circ}{\downarrow} p_i$.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
Let $i\in\{0,1,\dots,nh-1\}$.  Let $\alpha\in D_i-\downarrow a_i$ have a unique lower cover $\beta$ in $P^P$ such that $d_{i+1}\le\beta$ and $d_i\nleq\beta$.

Then $\alpha(p_i)>d_i(p_i)$; and $\alpha(p_i)$ has a lower cover $\beta(p_i)$ in $P$ such that $d_{i+1}(p_i)\le\beta(p_i)$ and $d_i(p_i)\nleq\beta(p_i)$.  

Now assume $|\{C_p\mid p\in P\}|=1$.  For $p\in\overset{\circ}{\downarrow} p_i$, $\alpha(p)\le d_{i+1}(p_i)$.  If $\alpha$ is a maximal element of
$$
\{a\in D_i-\downarrow a_i\mid a\text{ has a unique lower cover }b\text{ in }P^P
$$
$$
\text{ such that }d_{i+1}\le b\text{ and }d_i\nleq b\}\text{,}
$$
\noindent then $\alpha>a_i$ and $\alpha(p)=d_{i+1}(p_i)$ for all $p\in\overset{\circ}{\downarrow} p_i$.
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
Assume that $P$ and $\overline P$ are trebled ordered sets.  Let 
$$
\phi:P^P\to\overline P^{\overline P}
$$
\noindent be an order-isomorphism.

For $j\in\{0,1,\dots,nh\}$, let $\overline d_j:=\phi(d_j)$.  (Note that $nh=\overline n\overline h$.)  Let $\overline D:=\{\overline d_0,\overline d_1,\dots,\overline d_{nh}\}$.  Fix $i\in\{0,1,\dots,nh-1\}$ and assume $\phi[D_i]=\overline D_i$.

Assume that $|\{C_p\mid p\in P\}|=1$.

Then $a_i$ is the largest element $\alpha\in D_i$ that has a unique lower cover $\beta\in P^P$ such that $d_{i+1}\le\beta$ and $d_i\nleq\beta$.

Furthermore, $\overline a_i$ is the largest element $\overline\alpha\in\overline D_i$ that has a unique lower cover $\overline\beta\in{\overline P}^{\overline P}$ such that $\overline d_{i+1}\le\overline\beta$ and $\overline d_i\nleq\overline\beta$.

We have $\phi(a_i)=\overline a_i$ and $\phi[D_{i+1}]=\overline D_{i+1}$.
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
Assume $P$ and $\overline P$ are trebled ordered sets.  Assume that
$$
|\{C_p\mid p\in P\}|=1.
$$

Then $\phi[D_{nh}]=\overline D_{\overline n\overline h}$.
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
